headline: Approved one-year extension for Greenhouse Dispensary at 711 Kingstown Rd.; recommended Town Council ban data centers, 6-1 vote.
summary: Items covered an extension for a cannabis retail store at 711 Kingstown Rd. and a Form Based Code for areas near Dale Carlia Corner. Members directed staff to draft a negative motion on the Peacedale Preserve zoning amendment and voted 6-1 to recommend a data center ban.
decisions: Approved a one-year extension, to December 16, 2027, of the Special Use Permit and Preliminary Plan for the Greenhouse Dispensary at 711 Kingstown Rd., by unanimous vote.
Directed the Planning Director to create a negative motion on the Peacedale Preserve Special Management District zoning map and text amendment, by unanimous vote.
Approved the draft letter of support for the Form Based Code, with changes made at the meeting, by unanimous vote.
Recommended that the Town Council adopt a ban on data centers, consistent with the Comprehensive Community Plan, by a 6-1 vote (Monaco opposed).

decision_evidence.quote: The South Kingstown Planning Board hereby re-adopts the motion that was made at the August 25, 2026, Planning Board meeting to grant a one-year extension to the December 16, 2025, approval of the Special Use Permit for a Marijuana Retail Facility and Preliminary Plan for the Greenshouse Dispensary Minor Land Development project, now expiring December 16, 2027.

The South Kingstown Planning Board hereby directs the Planning Director, Jamie Rabbitt, to create a negative motion, reflecting the discussion of the Planning Board members in regard to "The Peace Dale Preserve Special Management District — proposed Zoning Ordinance Text & Map Amendment."

The South Kingstown Planning Board hereby approves the draft letter of support for the Form Based Code, with tonight's changes, to go to the Town Council prior to the Public Hearing to be held on September 14, 2026.

The South Kingstown Planning Board hereby recommends that the South Kingstown Town Council adopt the proposal to ban data centers, and feels it is consistent with the Town's Comprehensive Community Plan.

plain_text:
Town of South Kingstown   
Planning Board   
Work Session  Meeting Minutes 
Thursday, September 10, 2026 at 6:30 PM   
South Kingstown Town Hall, Town Council Chambers 
180 High Street, Wakefield, RI 02879 
www.southkingstownri.gov  
Maria H. Mack, Chair 
Susan Axelrod, Vice Chair 
Elizabeth Karp, Secretary 
Paul Jordan 
Armand Monaco 
Robyn Pothier 
Kaiper Wilson 
 
A. Call to Order & Roll Call: 
Ms. Mack called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. 
 
ROLL CALL: 
Present:  Susan Axelrod, Paul Jordan, Liz Karp, Armand Monaco, Robyn Pothier, Kaiper Wilson, and Maria Mack. 
Absent:  None 
 
Also Present: James Rabbitt, Director of Planning; Brian Wagner, Deputy Director of Planning; Lynn Smith, Planning 
Associate; and Andrew Teitz, Special Legal Counsel. 
 
Ms. Mack requested to move Item #2 up on the agenda, the request was agreed upon unanimously. 
B. Subdivision & Land Development Projects 
 1. EXTENSION REQUEST - Greenhouse Dispensary.  711 Kingstown Rd.; Plat 57-2, Lot 76. Request for a 1-year 
extension of the December 2025 Preliminary Plan & Special Use Permit Approvals for a Minor Land 
Development Project with Unified Development Review for a cannabis retail store. 
Mr. Wagner explained why this application is back before the Planning Board.   
The applicant and his attorney were unable to attend tonight's meeting.  
 
The following motion, made by Ms. Wilson, duly seconded by Ms. Karp, passed by unanimous vote. 
Motion: The South Kingstown Planning Board hereby re-adopts the motion that was made at the August 25, 2026, 
Planning Board meeting to grant a one-year extension to the December 16, 2025, approval of the Special Use Permit for 
a Marijuana Retail Facility and Preliminary Plan for the Greenshouse Dispensary Minor Land Development project, now 
expiring December 16, 2027."  
 
C. Recommendations to Town Council: 
 1. ZONING MAP AND TEXT AMENDMENT — "The Peacedale Preserve Special Management District." Tax 
Assessor's Map 33, Lot 30. An application to amend the Town's Zoning Ordinance to create a new zoning 
district allowing new or expanded commercial, residential and recreational land usage. Applicant/Owner 
BWJW, LLC, 371 Rose Hill Road, Wakefield, RI  02879. 
Ms. Mack referenced information provided by Mr. Rabbitt giving two options; and stated that the Board had requested 
a denial motion based on the discussion at the previous meeting. 
Discussion ensued.  
 
Brad Waugh, owner/applicant, and Patrick Dougherty, attorney for the applicant, were also in attendance. 
 
The following motion, made by Mr. Jordan, duly seconded by Ms. Wilson, passed by unanimous vote. 
Motion: The South Kingstown Planning Board hereby directs the Planning Director, Jamie Rabbitt, to create a negative 
motion, reflecting the discussion of the Planning Board members in regard to "The Peace Dale Preserve Special 
Management District — proposed Zoning Ordinance Text & Map Amendment."
2. ZONING MAP & TEXT AMENDMENT - Old Tower Hill Road Neighborhood Project, Form-Based Code. Review 
and action on an advisory recommendation to the Town Council regarding proposed revisions to the S.K. 
Zoning Ordinance focussing on the Commercial Highway District and other areas surrounding Dale Carlia 
Corner, Old Tower Hill Road, Kingstown Road and Main Street.  See Proposed Code At: 
 https://www.southkingstownri.gov/othr-fbc 
Mr. Rabbitt gave the Planning Board members an update on the schedule for the Form Based Code going before the 
Town Council. 
Discussion ensued with suggestions/revisions to the code. 
 
The following motion, made by Mr. Jordan, duly seconded by Ms. Axelrod, passed by unanimous vote. 
Motion: The South Kingstown Planning Board hereby approves the draft letter of support for the Form Based Code, with 
tonight's changes, to go to the Town Council prior to the Public Hearing to be held on September 14, 2026. 
 
 3. ZONING TEXT AMENDMENT - Data Centers. Discussion and action on a referral from Council for proposed 
revisions to the S.K. Zoning Ordinance including Appendix A (Use Codes) and Section 301 (Use Table) to 
define and prohibit data center development in all zoning districts 
Mr. Rabbitt informed the Board members that Town Council member, Michael Marran, reached out to the Town 
Solicitor regarding Data Centers.  Special Legal Counsel Amy Goins worked on the proposed Zoning Text Amendment, 
which has been distributed, clearly identifying that Data Centers will not be allowed in any district in South Kingstown.  
Discussion ensued. 
 
The following motion, made by Ms. Karp, duly seconded by Ms. Axelrod, passed by majority vote (Axelrod-aye; Jordan-
aye; Karp-aye; Mack-aye; Pothier-aye; Wilson-aye; Monaco-nay)  
Motion: "The South Kingstown Planning Board hereby recommends that the South Kingstown Town Council adopt the 
proposal to ban data centers, and feels it is consistent with the Town's Comprehensive Community Plan."  
D. Reports and Special Items: 
Mr. Wagner briefly discussed the Grow Smart letter in support of the Form Based Code, distributed to the Planning 
Board members. 
 
Mr. Rabbitt informed the Board of a meeting he attended with RI Housing and the new program being started called 
Housing Champions, for municipalities to join.      
 
Ms. Wilson stated her concern with zoning issues that come before the Planning Board.  Mr. Rabbitt suggested this be 
added to the next work session for discussion (10/6). 
 
Mr. Rabbitt reminded the Board that he and Mr. Teitz will be presenting the Form Based Code to the Town Council on 
September 14, 2026. 
 
Ms. Mack informed the Board and Staff that DEM, the University of Maryland, and the Nature Conservancy, are 
conducting an in-depth scientific study with regard to the forests in RI.  
A Zoom meeting organized by the RI Resource Conservation and Development Area Council will be held on November 
18, 2026, at 7:00 p.m., and she will have Mr. Rabbitt distribute the electronic version of the meeting. 
E. Report of Administrative Officer: 
Sept. 14th FBC with TC.   
 
mm- dem univ of maryland nature concervacy, in-depth study on the forest in RI 11/18 @ 7:00 p.m.
F. Adjournment: 
Upon Motion made by Mr. Jordan, duly seconded by Ms. Wilson, the meeting was adjourned at 7:37 p.m., by unanimous 
vote.
